issues.description: The problem statement requires a SealSaloon method named checkOrderReady() (used/mentioned throughout the spec and UML) but the solution implements this functionality in a method named processOrders() and orderMeal() calls processOrders(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about which method to implement and violates the expected API described in the problem.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name with the problem statement. Either rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady() and have orderMeal() call checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() that delegates to processOrders(). Update any references so the API matches the UML and textual specification.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual requirements) specifies a method named checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon to attempt to serve queued orders. In the provided solution the same functionality is implemented under the different identifier processOrders(). This naming divergence for a core behavior method (checking and serving orders) can confuse students mapping the requirement (implement checkOrderReady) to the solution or tests that refer to checkOrderReady.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that invokes processOrders()) so the implementation name matches the problem specification and test expectations.
